units.title: Letters, vowels and the umlaut
goals: Explain how German spelling records sound, and name the few things spelling does not show
Say the name of every letter, including 'ä', 'ö', 'ü' and 'ß', and spell your own name aloud
Tell a long vowel from a short one by its spelling: a doubled vowel, a silent 'h', 'ie' or a doubled consonant
Say the umlaut vowels and the diphthongs 'ei', 'au' and 'eu', and tell 'ie' from 'ei'
Recognize the weak unstressed 'e' and the vowel-like 'r' of '-er'
grammar: The alphabet: 26 letters and their names, plus 'ä', 'ö', 'ü' and 'ß'; spelling aloud and the spelling alphabet
Five vowel letters, each with a long and a short sound; pure vowels with no glide
The umlaut: 'ä', 'ö' and 'ü' as vowels of their own, not stress marks
Vowel length from spelling: doubled vowels, the silent 'h', 'ie', doubled consonants, and where spelling does not decide
Diphthongs 'ei' and 'ai', 'au', 'eu' and 'äu'; the weak 'e' [ə]; '-er' [ɐ] and 'r' after a long vowel
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each vowel and spelling rule
letter names and spelling your own name aloud
pairs of words that differ by one vowel

units.title: Consonants and the letter 'ß'
goals: Read every consonant spelling of German aloud, including 'ch', 'sch', 'sp', 'st', 'w', 'v', 'z' and 'j'
Choose between 'ß' and 'ss' by the vowel before them, following the rule of the 1996 spelling reform
Say the two sounds of 'ch' and know which letters before it choose each one
Apply final devoicing: 'b', 'd' and 'g' at the end of a syllable
Read aloud a German word never seen before
grammar: 's' [z] before a vowel and [s] elsewhere; 'ss' and 'ß' [s], and the rule that chooses between them
'sch' [ʃ]; 'sp' and 'st' at the start of a word or word part [ʃp], [ʃt]
'ch' [ç] and [x], 'chs' [ks], and '-ig' at the end of a word
'w' [v], 'v' [f], 'j' [j], 'z' and 'tz' [ts], 'qu', 'pf', 'ng', 'nk', 'ph', 'th', 'dt'
'r' before a vowel [ʁ]; final devoicing of 'b', 'd' and 'g'
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each consonant and spelling rule
common nouns for food, the street and the day
pairs of words that differ by one consonant

units.title: Stress, compound words and capital letters
goals: Find the stressed syllable of a native German word: the first syllable of its stem
Recognize the unstressed prefixes and the stressed loanword endings that move the stress
Split a compound word into its parts, find its main stress and its gender
Know which words German writes with a capital letter
grammar: Syllables and stress; native words stress the first syllable of the stem
Unstressed prefixes 'be-', 'ge-', 'er-', 'ver-', 'zer-', 'ent-', 'emp-'; stressed prefixes such as 'an-' and 'auf-'
Loanword endings that carry the stress ('-ion', '-tät', '-ie', '-ieren', '-ik', '-ent', '-ei'), and foreign spellings kept in loanwords
Compound words: the last part gives the meaning and the gender, the first part carries the stress, and linking 's' or 'n'
The glottal stop, and capital letters for every noun and for 'Sie'
vocabulary_themes: loanwords with the stress on a later syllable
compound words built from words already known

units.title: How German works: the big picture
goals: Name the parts of speech and the terms of grammar used in this course, in English and German
Explain how a German sentence is built: the verb in second place, the verb bracket and the verb at the end of a subordinate clause
Understand the three genders and predict the gender of many nouns from their endings
Understand what a case is, what the four cases do, and why German can change its word order
Know the map of the verb system and the forms of address 'du', 'ihr' and 'Sie'
grammar: Parts of speech and the grammar vocabulary of the course
The verb-second rule, questions with the verb first, the verb bracket, and no helper verb like English 'do'
Gender (masculine, neuter, feminine), number, and the endings that predict gender; 'der', 'das', 'die', 'ein', 'eine'
The four cases and what each one does, with the definite article in every case as a map
Verbs: infinitive, stem, ending and conjugation; the tenses, moods and passive the course teaches; the auxiliaries 'haben', 'sein' and 'werden'
The subject pronouns and the forms of address; negation with 'nicht' and 'kein'
vocabulary_themes: the words for the parts of speech and the terms of grammar
the articles and the smallest function words ('und', 'nicht')

units.title: Greetings and introductions
goals: Greet people at different times of day and say goodbye
Introduce yourself, ask someone's name and say you are pleased to meet them
Say where you are from and what nationality you are
Choose 'du', 'ihr' or 'Sie' for the person you are speaking to
Say what each greeting literally means and how it is used
grammar: Subject pronouns 'ich', 'du', 'er', 'sie', 'es', 'wir', 'ihr', 'sie' and 'Sie'
The present of 'sein' ('ich bin', 'du bist', 'er ist', 'wir sind', 'ihr seid', 'sie sind')
'heißen' and 'kommen' as the first regular verbs; 'Ich komme aus' plus a country
Nationality nouns with no article ('Ich bin Amerikaner', 'Ich bin Amerikanerin')
Fixed formulas: 'Wie geht's?', 'Wie geht es Ihnen?', 'Freut mich', 'Mein Name ist ...'

units.title: The present tense, questions and 'nicht'
goals: Conjugate regular verbs and 'haben' in the present
Use the verbs that change their stem vowel in the 'du' and 'er' forms
Ask yes or no questions and questions with a question word, and answer with 'ja', 'nein' or 'doch'
Negate a sentence with 'nicht'
Say which languages you speak and what you like doing
grammar: Regular present endings, with the extra 'e' after 't' and 'd' and the short 'du' form after 's', 'ß' and 'z'
The present of 'haben'
Stem-vowel change from 'e' to 'i' or 'ie' ('du sprichst', 'er liest')
Questions with the verb first and with 'was', 'wer', 'wo', 'wie' and 'woher'; 'doch' against a negative
The place of 'nicht'; 'gern' with a verb

units.title: Numbers, time and days
goals: Count from 0 to 100
Say your age and your phone number
Tell the time with the 24-hour clock and in everyday speech
Name the days of the week, the parts of the day and the months
grammar: Numbers 0 to 100: units before tens ('einundzwanzig'), 'eins' and 'ein', 'sechzehn', 'siebzehn', 'dreißig'
Age with 'sein' ('Ich bin dreißig Jahre alt')
The time: 'Viertel nach', 'Viertel vor', 'halb' ('halb drei' is half past two), 'um' plus a time
Days of the week and months, all masculine; the parts of the day; 'morgens' and 'abends'
vocabulary_themes: clock times and the parts of the day

units.title: Food, drinks and the accusative
goals: Order food and drinks in a café or restaurant and ask for the bill
Use the accusative for the object of a verb
Say what you want with 'möchte' and what you like with 'mögen'
Negate a noun with 'kein'
Use 'es gibt' and the accusative prepositions 'für', 'ohne', 'durch', 'gegen' and 'um'
grammar: The accusative: 'den' and 'einen' for the masculine, the other forms unchanged
The negative article 'kein' and when to use 'kein' or 'nicht'
'es gibt' plus the accusative; stem changes in 'essen' and 'nehmen'
'mögen' in the present, and 'möchte' as its polite form for wanting
Accusative prepositions; quantities with no word for 'of' ('eine Tasse Kaffee')
vocabulary_themes: café and restaurant phrases ('die Speisekarte', 'die Rechnung', 'Zahlen, bitte')

units.title: Family, plurals and possessive articles
goals: Talk about your family and your pets
Form the plural of nouns and know the five plural patterns
Use the possessive articles in the nominative and accusative
Say whose something is with 'von' or a name with 's'
grammar: The five plural patterns: '-e', '-er', '-(e)n', '-s' and no ending, with or without an umlaut
The plural article 'die' and plurals with no article
Possessive articles 'mein', 'dein', 'sein', 'ihr', 'unser', 'euer', 'Ihr' with the endings of 'ein'
'von' plus a name, and a name with 's' ('Annas Mutter')

units.title: Daily routine and separable verbs
goals: Describe your daily routine
Use separable verbs and put their prefix at the end of the clause
Put a time expression first and the verb second
Say how often you do something
grammar: Separable verbs: the stressed prefix at the end of the main clause; inseparable verbs and 'frühstücken'
Inversion after a time expression ('Um sieben stehe ich auf')
Stem-vowel change from 'a' to 'ä' ('fahren', 'schlafen', 'anfangen')
Frequency and sequence words ('immer', 'oft', 'manchmal', 'nie', 'zuerst', 'dann')
vocabulary_themes: home and work ('zu Hause', 'nach Hause', 'die Arbeit')

units.title: Modal verbs: ability, obligation and permission
goals: Say what you can, must, want to, may and are supposed to do
Put the infinitive at the end of the sentence after a modal verb
Tell 'nicht müssen' from 'nicht dürfen'
State rules with 'man'
Talk about hobbies and free time
grammar: The present of 'können', 'müssen', 'wollen', 'dürfen', 'sollen' and 'mögen'
The modal verb with the infinitive at the end, and separable verbs after a modal
'nicht müssen' against 'nicht dürfen'; modal verbs with no infinitive
The indefinite pronoun 'man'; 'möchte' compared with 'will'

units.title: Places, directions and the dative
goals: Ask the way and give directions
Use the dative after the dative prepositions
Tell 'wo', 'wohin' and 'woher' apart, and 'nach' from 'zu'
Give an instruction with the 'Sie' form of the imperative
grammar: The dative of the articles, of 'kein' and of the possessives, and '-n' on the dative plural
Dative prepositions 'aus', 'bei', 'mit', 'nach', 'seit', 'von', 'zu', 'gegenüber'
Contractions 'zum', 'zur', 'beim', 'vom' and 'am'
The 'Sie' imperative ('Gehen Sie geradeaus'); 'mit' plus a means of transport

units.title: Shopping, clothes and object pronouns
goals: Shop for clothes, ask about sizes and prices, and try things on
Replace a noun with an accusative pronoun of the right gender
Ask 'which one?' with 'welcher' and point out with 'dieser'
Say prices in euros and cents
grammar: Accusative personal pronouns 'mich', 'dich', 'ihn', 'sie', 'es', 'uns', 'euch', 'sie', 'Sie'
'ein', 'kein' and the possessives used as pronouns ('Ich nehme einen', 'Das ist meins')
'welcher' and 'dieser' in the nominative and accusative
Prices with 'kosten'; colours after 'sein'; 'zu' plus an adjective

units.title: Home, rooms and where things are
goals: Describe a flat and its rooms
Say where something is with the dative and where it goes with the accusative
Use 'liegen', 'stehen' and 'hängen' for where things are
Talk about renting a flat
grammar: Two-way prepositions 'an', 'auf', 'hinter', 'in', 'neben', 'über', 'unter', 'vor', 'zwischen'
The dative for a location ('Wo?') and the accusative for a direction ('Wohin?')
Contractions 'im', 'am', 'ins', 'ans'
'liegen', 'stehen' and 'hängen' with the dative

units.title: Weather, plans and dates
goals: Talk about the weather and the seasons
Make plans and invite someone
Say the date with ordinal numbers
Use 'um', 'am' and 'im' for times, days and months
grammar: 'es' as a placeholder subject ('es regnet', 'es ist kalt')
The present tense with a time word for the future
Ordinal numbers and dates ('der dritte Mai', 'am dritten Mai')
Time prepositions 'um', 'am' and 'im'; suggestions with 'Wollen wir ...?' and 'Hast du Lust?'

units.title: A1 consolidation
goals: Hold a short conversation about yourself, your family, your day and your plans
Use the nominative, accusative and dative correctly with articles, pronouns and prepositions
Put the verb in the right place in statements, questions and sentences with a modal or separable verb
Join main clauses with 'und', 'aber', 'oder', 'denn' and 'sondern'
Offer or accept the switch from 'Sie' to 'du'
grammar: Review: the three cases taught so far and the verb positions
'denn' and 'sondern' as linking words, and 'denn' as a particle in questions
Indefinite pronouns 'jemand', 'niemand', 'etwas' and 'nichts'; 'jeder' as a 'der' word and as a pronoun
Offering 'du' ('Wollen wir uns duzen?')

units.title: The compound past with 'haben'
goals: Talk about what you did with the compound past
Form regular, strong and mixed past participles
Put the past participle at the end of the sentence
Use 'schon' and 'noch nicht'
grammar: The compound past: 'haben' plus the past participle at the end; its use as the past of speech
Regular participles 'ge-' plus stem plus '-t' or '-et'
Strong participles in '-en' with a vowel change ('gegessen', 'getrunken', 'geschrieben') and mixed participles ('gebracht', 'gedacht')
Past time words ('gestern', 'letzte Woche', 'schon', 'noch nicht')

units.title: The compound past with 'sein', and verbs with prefixes
goals: Choose 'sein' or 'haben' for the compound past
Form the past participles of separable verbs
Form the past participles of inseparable verbs and verbs in '-ieren'
Tell the story of a journey
grammar: 'sein' for a change of place or state, and for 'sein', 'bleiben' and 'passieren'
'ge-' between prefix and stem in separable verbs ('aufgestanden')
No 'ge-' with inseparable prefixes or '-ieren' ('besucht', 'studiert'), explained by the stress

units.title: Childhood and school: 'war', 'hatte' and the modals in the past
goals: Talk about your childhood and school days
Use the simple past of 'sein', 'haben' and the modal verbs
Say how long ago something happened with 'vor'
Say years aloud
grammar: The simple past of 'sein' and 'haben'
The simple past of the modal verbs, with no umlaut ('konnte', 'musste', 'durfte')
'es gab'; 'vor' plus the dative for 'ago'; 'als Kind'
Numbers above a hundred, and years ('neunzehnhundertneunundachtzig', 'im Jahr 2010')

units.title: Gifts and celebrations: the dative for people
goals: Give, show and send things to people
Use the dative personal pronouns
Put a dative and an accusative object in the right order
Use the verbs that take a dative object
Congratulate someone and thank them
grammar: Dative personal pronouns 'mir', 'dir', 'ihm', 'ihr', 'uns', 'euch', 'ihnen', 'Ihnen'
Verbs with a dative person and an accusative thing, and the order of the two objects
Verbs with a dative object ('helfen', 'danken', 'gefallen', 'gehören', 'schmecken', 'passen', 'antworten')
'Wie geht es dir?', 'Das gefällt mir' and 'Mir ist kalt' explained

units.title: Describing things: adjective endings
goals: Describe people and things with an adjective before the noun
Choose the adjective ending after 'der' words
Choose the adjective ending after 'ein', 'kein' and the possessive articles
Ask 'what kind of?' with 'was für ein'
grammar: The principle: when the article does not show the case and gender, the adjective does
Adjective endings after 'der' words in the nominative, accusative and dative
Adjective endings after 'ein' words in the nominative, accusative and dative
'was für ein'; ordinals, 'letzte' and 'nächste' with their endings

units.title: Comparing things and places
goals: Compare people, things and places
Form the comparative and superlative, including the umlauted and irregular ones
Use 'als' and 'so ... wie'
Talk about the geography of Germany
grammar: Comparative '-er' and superlative 'am -sten'
Umlaut in short adjectives ('älter', 'größer'); irregular forms ('besser', 'mehr', 'lieber', 'höher', 'näher')
'als' and 'so ... wie'; 'immer' plus a comparative
Comparative and superlative before a noun, with adjective endings

units.title: Health, the body and the imperative
goals: Name the parts of the body and say what hurts
Talk to a doctor or a pharmacist
Give instructions and advice with the imperative and 'sollen'
Say how long something has been going on with 'seit'
grammar: The imperative for 'du', 'ihr', 'Sie' and 'wir', and of 'sein'
Softening an imperative with 'bitte' and the particle 'mal'
'wehtun' with the dative; 'sollen' for advice
'seit' with the present tense

units.title: Reflexive verbs
goals: Use reflexive pronouns in the accusative and the dative
Describe your morning routine with reflexive verbs
Tell verbs that are always reflexive from verbs used reflexively
Say what you look forward to and what annoys you
grammar: Reflexive pronouns in the accusative and the dative ('Ich wasche mich', 'Ich wasche mir die Hände')
Body parts with the article, not a possessive
Verbs that are always reflexive; 'sich vorstellen' with the accusative and with the dative
The position of 'sich'; reflexive verbs in the compound past; 'sich' and 'einander' for each other

units.title: Reasons and opinions: subordinate clauses
goals: Give reasons with 'weil' and 'denn'
Report what someone thinks or says with 'dass'
Express conditions with 'wenn' and ask indirect questions with 'ob' and question words
Put the verb at the end of a subordinate clause, and start the main clause with its verb after one
grammar: The subordinate clause with the verb at the end, and the comma
'weil' against 'denn'; 'dass', 'wenn', 'ob'; indirect questions
A subordinate clause first, then the verb of the main clause
Separable verbs, modal verbs and the compound past in subordinate clauses

units.title: Travel, transport and putting things in place
goals: Buy a ticket and travel by train and public transport
Tell the verbs for putting something somewhere from the verbs for being somewhere
Use the time prepositions 'vor', 'in', 'ab', 'bis' and 'seit'
Use 'hin' and 'her' for direction

Time prepositions 'vor', 'in', 'ab', 'bis' and 'seit'
Separable travel verbs ('abfahren', 'einsteigen', 'aussteigen', 'umsteigen')
'hin' and 'her' ('Wo fährst du hin?')

units.title: Plans and wishes: 'werden', the future and polite requests
goals: Say what someone becomes with 'werden'
Talk about the future with 'werden' and with the present tense
Make polite requests with 'würde', 'könnte', 'hätte gern' and 'wäre'
Talk about your plans, training and career

The future with 'werden' plus the infinitive, and when the present tense is enough
Polite subjunctive II forms as a set: 'würde', 'könnte', 'hätte gern', 'wäre'

units.title: A2 consolidation
goals: Tell a connected story about a past trip with the compound past and the simple past of 'sein', 'haben' and the modals
Use all the verb positions, adjective endings and prepositions taught so far
Write a personal letter or email
Recommend places and say what is worth seeing
grammar: Review: the past tenses; every verb position in one table
Review: adjective endings after articles; prepositions by case
Personal letters and emails: 'Liebe Anna', 'Lieber Jonas', 'Viele Grüße'

units.title: Verbs with prepositions, and 'da' and 'wo' words
goals: Use verbs, adjectives and nouns with their fixed preposition and case
Refer to a thing with a 'da' word and to a person with a preposition and a pronoun
Ask about things with 'wo' words and about people with a preposition and 'wen' or 'wem'
Prepare for and talk about a job application
grammar: Fixed prepositions with verbs, adjectives and nouns ('warten auf', 'Angst haben vor', 'stolz auf')
'da' words ('darauf', 'daran', 'damit') against a preposition plus a pronoun
'wo' words in questions ('Worauf?', 'Woran?') against 'Auf wen?'
A 'da' word pointing forward to a 'dass' clause

units.title: The simple past: telling stories
goals: Form the simple past of weak, strong and mixed verbs
Learn a verb by its principal parts
Tell a story or a fairy tale in the simple past
Choose between 'als', 'wenn' and 'wann'
grammar: The simple past of weak verbs ('-te') and strong verbs (a new vowel, no ending in 'ich' and 'er'); mixed verbs
Principal parts and the vowel patterns of strong verbs
The simple past in writing and the compound past in speech
'als' for one past occasion, 'wenn' for a repeated one, 'wann' in questions

units.title: The genitive, and adjectives without an article
goals: Use the genitive to show possession and after the genitive prepositions
Choose the adjective ending when no article comes before it
Use adjectives as nouns ('der Bekannte', 'ein Bekannter')
Talk about food habits and health
grammar: The genitive articles and the '-s' or '-es' of masculine and neuter nouns; 'wessen'
Genitive prepositions 'wegen', 'trotz', 'während', 'statt', 'innerhalb', 'außerhalb', and the dative in everyday speech
Adjective endings with no article, and after 'einige', 'mehrere', 'viele' and 'wenige'
Adjectival nouns ('der Bekannte', 'die Deutschen')

units.title: People and relationships: relative clauses

Choose the relative pronoun by gender, number and case
Use a preposition before a relative pronoun
Use 'was' and 'wo' as relative words
Talk about character and relationships
grammar: Relative pronouns in all four cases ('der', 'den', 'dem', 'dessen'; 'denen', 'deren')
Case from the relative clause, gender and number from the noun; the verb at the end
A preposition before the relative pronoun ('mit dem')
'was' after 'alles', 'nichts', 'etwas' and a superlative; 'wo' for places

units.title: Subjunctive II: wishes, unreal conditions and advice

Talk about unreal conditions in the present
Express wishes and give advice
Make polite requests and suggestions

The forms 'wäre', 'hätte', 'könnte', 'müsste', 'dürfte', 'sollte'; the forms of 'wissen' and some strong verbs ('wüsste', 'gäbe', 'käme', 'ginge')
Unreal conditions with 'wenn' and with the verb first
Wishes ('Wenn ich doch ...', 'Ich wünschte') and advice ('An deiner Stelle würde ich ...', 'Du solltest ...')

units.title: The environment: infinitive clauses and 'lassen'

Express purpose with 'um ... zu' and 'damit'

Talk about the environment and saving energy

'ohne ... zu', 'statt ... zu'; 'brauchen' with 'nicht' or 'nur' plus 'zu'
'lassen': to let, to have something done, to leave

units.title: Life stories: the pluperfect and time clauses

Connect events with 'nachdem', 'bevor', 'seitdem', 'sobald', 'solange' and 'bis'
Tell the preposition 'nach', the conjunction 'nachdem' and the adverb 'danach' apart
Tell a life story

Time conjunctions and the sequence of tenses after 'nachdem'
Words with one spelling in several classes ('während', 'bis'), and 'nach', 'nachdem', 'danach'

units.title: How things are made: the passive

Use the passive with a modal verb
Name the doer with 'von' and the means with 'durch'

The three uses of 'werden'; 'man' as an alternative

units.title: Work, offices and formal letters

Write a formal letter or email
Deal with an office or authority
grammar: Weak masculine nouns ('der Kollege', 'den Kollegen'; 'der Herr', 'den Herrn')
Formal letters and emails: greetings, closings and requests with subjunctive II
'duzen' and 'siezen' at work

units.title: Word order in the middle of the sentence

Time, cause, manner and place

Opinion phrases ('meiner Meinung nach', 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass ...')

Distance yourself from a claim

Reported statements in the present, past and future; reported questions; reported commands with 'sollen'
'laut', 'zufolge' and 'angeblich'

units.title: What might have been: subjunctive II in the past

Compare with 'als ob' and 'als wenn'

Modal verbs with two infinitives ('hätte kommen sollen'), and their order in a subordinate clause
'als ob', 'als wenn' and 'als' with the verb next
'beinahe' and 'fast' with the past subjunctive

units.title: Science and research: the state passive and other passive forms

Use the passive with modal verbs in subordinate clauses

Adjectives in '-bar' and '-lich'; 'man' and reflexive verbs
The passive with modal verbs in subordinate clauses and in subjunctive II

units.title: Art and exhibitions: participles and extended attributes

Read an extended attribute and rewrite it as a relative clause
Understand 'zu' plus the present participle
Talk and write about art
